title: Hush Harbor · Part 1
idea: At 3:12 am the night ferry's engines cut out and the captain whispers one rule into the radio: nobody makes a sound; every passenger is already taking off their shoes. Three rules (phones off, no shoes on the metal deck, never touch the railing, whatever you see out there: a fox with a lantern on a buoy in the fog). Something big slides along the hull and stops under your feet, listening. Two rows ahead a little girl opens a music box and it starts to play; her mother is asleep, and under the floor it turns toward the music. Stopping it means crossing the metal deck, throwing it means touching the railing. STOP or THROW?
hook: It's 3:12 AM on the night ferry, and every engine just cut out. The captain whispers one rule into the radio: from now on, nobody makes a sound. And every passenger around you is already taking off their shoes.
caption:
3:12 AM. The night ferry stops in the fog. 🌫️
The captain whispers one rule: nobody makes a sound.
And everyone around you is already taking off their shoes. 👟

Then a little girl opens her music box. 🎶

Stop it and you cross the metal deck. Throw it and you touch the railing.
Comment STOP or THROW. Part 2 follows the most-commented answer. 🦊🏮
first_comment: STOP or THROW? And why were the locals already barefoot? 🦊🏮
